#2731. Ball State women's basketball falls to No. 7 Louisville in encouraging outing

MUNCIE — Nearly 13 years ago, on Dec. 18, 2013, Ball State women's basketball hosted No. 7 Louisville, marking the first time ever that the Cardinals hosted a top-10 team in Worthen Arena. Ball State lost that game by 38 points.

On Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, Ball State women's basketball hosted a top-10 team for the second time in program history. Coincidentally, it was Louisville again, and in an even bigger coincidence, the visiting Cardinals were ranked No. 7 again.

Ball State fared much better than it did 13 years ago, but ultimately couldn't keep up with its elite competition, falling to Louisville in a 94-73 result.

Despite the 21-point deficit on the scoreboard at the end of the night, Ball State head coach Brady Sallee was very pleased with his team's performance and approach to the game following a tough loss to High Point in their last game.

"How much fun was that?" Sallee said. "I'm telling you, those are the ones I like to play. Man, they're good, but I told this group, I think we were good too. I can get down with that team that I just watched play. That team last Saturday, I was about ready to take them back to Enterprise Rent-A-Car and trade it out. But this group, man, I can get down with that. I think we got so much better in the last three or four days."

More: Ball State women's basketball falls to High Point in mid-major battle

Ball State's shortcomings in this loss were obvious — the home Cardinals were physically overmatched by the visitors. After all, Louisville is a top-10 team for a reason, and they looked every bit the part of a Final Four contender in their win at Worthen Arena.

The visiting Cardinals used their size and length to fluster Ball State's offense, finishing with 12 steals and seven blocks as a team. Many of their blocks came on Ball State 3-point attempts where Louisville's players barely had to jump.

"They're very athletic," Ball State freshman Lilli Barnes said. "They're big, they're tall, they're lengthy, so they're very active on defense and can read everything."

In spite of the physical mismatch, Ball State's players never looked like they were intimidated by the competition. Much like Sallee, they embraced the opportunity to compete with an elite opponent and see how they measure up against a program that has become a Sweet 16 regular in the 2020s. That fearless mentality began in practice, where the Cardinals had a much better week after Sallee called out their preparation following their loss to High Point.

"I think it's just the mindset we go into practice with," junior Grace Kingery said. "We have to take everything seriously, especially when we go through scout and knowing the personnel and stuff, so I think it's just being locked in, especially at shootaround too."

Barnes made her first collegiate start and led Ball State with 22 points on 7-of-10 field goal shooting while also pulling down a team-high seven rebounds. The heralded freshman out of Valparaiso has wasted no time in establishing herself as a rising star for Ball State, and it's become clear through three games that she will have a major impact on the Cardinals' success this season. Achieving that status often comes with a lot of pressure, especially for such a young player, but Barnes is built for the moment.

"I think before every game, there's a little bit of nerves whether you're starting or just on the bench," Barnes said. "Once the ball goes up, just playing and getting a feel for the game, I've been playing all my life, so it just comes as the game goes on."

Zhen Verburgt finished second on the team in scoring with 13 points, while Kingery followed with 12 points.

Ball State benefitted from a large and loud home crowd, particularly a very full and raucous student section. Sallee was very complimentary of the student section's energy throughout the game, and the players agreed that it played a part in their own energetic performance.

"It helped a lot," Kingery said. "It was so much fun, especially when we cut the lead down to within 10. It was great."

Sallee professed postgame that he is not a fan of moral victories and is more concerned with his team's process of getting better. This week, he felt that their process was sound and that the team was ready to play against an elite Louisville team. Although the final score was lopsided against them, it was a good night for Ball State women's basketball.

"I think it's important that, in your own locker room, you define success for yourself," Sallee said. "You don't necessarily chase wins and losses — those become byproducts of doing everything right. For us, we work and we walk about it a lot, about what success means to us. We could play Ave Maria Technical State College of the who-knows-what and win, but I don't know that, if your process isn't good, would you be happy with that win? It's just fool's gold."

Ball State's next opponent will be much tougher than the fictional Ave Maria Tech State, as the Cardinals are set to host yet another ranked team when No. 21 Illinois comes to Muncie on Wednesday, Nov. 18. The Cardinals and Fighting Illini will tip off at 6:30 p.m. ET at Worthen Arena.

#2730. NFL news, live updates: Rams officially place Puka Nacua on injured reserve with knee injury

The 2026 NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and we're on to Week 10, where we'll see a couple of players in new uniforms this week — and some in their old uniforms.

Kirk Cousins rejoined the Minnesota Vikings this week via a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. He will presumably don purple this weekend against the Green Bay Packers — the very team he last faced with Minnesota, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. He'll look to give the offense a much-needed boost to complement Brian Flores' defense after the team's 6-2 start.

With the trade of Cousins, the Raiders officially named 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza as their starter moving forward. He'll face a tough schedule to kick off his career as a starting quarterback, with the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on deck in Weeks 10 and 11.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 10.

After a great deal of speculation was made that Jonathan Taylor could be moved ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly standing pat.

The team will not trade him ahead of the deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Tuesday afternoon.

Pelissero reported that the Colts had received multiple offers for Taylor of a second-round pick-plus, but instead, the team will move forward with him as a foundational piece within the locker room as they look to rebuild.

Any concerns that Justin Herbert might be limited by his injured left middle finger were likely put to rest with the quarterback not listed on the Los Angeles Chargers injury report for Thursday.

After getting injured and leaving during the fourth quarter of the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, imaging exams showed no fracture in Herbert's finger.

However, the Chargers' injury report was extensive with 18 players listed, including receiver Ladd McConkey (back), edge rusher Khalil Mack (rest) and linebacker Daiyan Henley (personal), who did not practice. Tight end David Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant.

The Chargers (0-8) will try to get their first win of the season on Monday night versus the Baltimore Ravens (4-5).

The Los Angeles Rams have reportedly placed All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve with a knee injury suffered last week, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

That will have him out for the next four games, after Sean McVay previously noted Nacua would miss a "significant" period of time with the injury. It took some time to play out, however, as the team dealt with what McVay called "roster semantics."

Kirk Cousins' return to Minnesota will be marked with a familiar number: The team announced Thursday that their new quarterback will wear No. 8 going forward. That's the number Cousin wore with the Vikings when he played for them from 2018-2023.

Minnesota safety Jakobe Thomas, who was wearing No. 8 earlier this season, will switch to No. 6 to accommodate Cousins return.

Riley Patterson will kick for the Ravens this week in their Monday Night Football matchup with the Chargers, according to the NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. Patterson spent the past two seasons with the Dolphins, but was released last month.

The Patriots will be playing the Lions in Munich, Germany, on Sunday.

Running back TreVeyon Henderson did not practice on Wednesday, and with an upcoming flight across the pond, the team has already ruled him out.

Henderson was listed on the injury report as dealing with an illness. The running back revealed last Friday that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms." Henderson was hospitalized, but has said that test results have been positive and reassuring.

Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson also didn't practice on Wednesday due to a knee injury, but has not yet been ruled out, though he is expected to miss a few weeks.

Sean McVay delivered a mix bag of news Wednesday regarding injuries to the team's top two receivers.

Davante Adams could be back sooner than expected from a hamstring injury, potentially in Week 13 vs. the Chiefs. Puka Nacua, meanwhile, will remain sidelined for a "significant period of time" with knee and toe injuries.

Etienne has been out since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury and has since been on injured reserve.

His return to practice opens his 21-day window to return to action, meaning the Saints have three weeks to activate him to the 53-man roster or shut him down for the season.

Skattebo missed Sunday's win over the Eagles coming out of the team's bye week. The running back practiced this week, which sets him up for a return Thursday night against the Commanders.

McCarthy was sacked five times in the game and suffered a rib injury that briefly took him out of action. He would return and finished 12-for-19 for 127 yards passing.

"I feel really good," McCarthy said this week. "Obviously, Sunday, it's football, it's a physical game, but just credit to the athletic training staff, getting me back to feeling really good as quick as possible."

The 49ers acquired Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline because of the various injuries the team has at the position.

San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Wednesday that Mike Evans remains week-to-week due to an Achilles injury. At this point, he has not been added to IR, so Evans could suit up this week against the Cowboys, but he is starting the week by not practicing.

Shanahan added that currently there is no timeline for Evans' return.

The Rams are expected to be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for more than a month after suffering two knee sprains in the team's most recent game.

Nacua, who would normally be added to IR to free up a roster spot, won't be, according to head coach Sean McVay. L.A. is still expecting Nacua to miss extended time, but NFL teams are only allowed eight player activations from IR per season.

If Nacua gets added, with the intention of activating him in December, he would take up an activation from another player that the Rams were planning on activating, which would rule them out for the year.

L.A. currently has WR Davante Adams, G Justin Dedich, DT Poona Ford and DE Kobie Turner on IR and the Rams likely want to be able to activate all of them later this year. Los Angeles has already used four activations with EDGE Myles Garrett, TE Terrance Ferguson, OT Keagan Trost and RB Ronnie Rivers.

The 49ers acquired Keenan Allen ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline to help bolster the banged-up wide receiver room.

The only problem is that Allen could still miss time this season. Kyle Shanahan acknowledged to reporters on Wednesday that the veteran wideout could still face league discipline this season stemming from his DUI in August.

According to the current CBA, a violation of the league's substance-abuse policy, which would include a DUI, comes with a minimum three-game suspension. Additionally, Allen's BAC was so high that the league can increase the suspension if it so chooses.

The league has reportedly been waiting for the DUI case against Allen to play out legally before issuing the suspension.

At 3-6, and with a rash of injuries — including one to their most recent QB1 — the Arizona Cardinals are turning to rookie Carson Beck.

Arizona benched and then traded Jacoby Brissett. His replacement, Gardner Minshew, suffered a UCL injury this past week in Seattle during a loss to the Seahawks.

In their absence, the No. 65 overall pick in this year's draft is getting the nod in the desert.

Beck will make his first career NFL start on Sunday when the Los Angeles Rams come to town, head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday. The former Georgia and Miami star will be tasked with moving the ball against a defense that features premier edge rusher Myles Garrett and stout defensive tackle Aaron Donald. Beck will have to do so with a thin receiving corps.

Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy announced on Wednesday that the team is opening the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Derrick Harmon.

The 23-year-old defender has been sidelined because of a sprained foot he suffered against the Bengals in Week 4. In limited action this season, he has 12 tackles, including 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble.

Pittsburgh is allowing the seventh-fewest yards per game and the third-fewest rush yards per game this season.

The Patriots will cross the pond this weekend to take on the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, on Sunday morning.

New England wide receiver A.J. Brown will travel with the team, head coach Mike Vrabel said. While this doesn't automatically mean he will play in Sunday's game, Vrabel noted it gives him the chance.

Brown has missed the Patriots' last two games due to a knee injury. The wide receiver has only played in three games for New England this season, as he missed the early part of the season because of a sprained ankle in Week 1.

The wide receiver has caught nine of his 20 targets for 101 yards. Brown has yet to score a touchdown this year.

Tuesday's trade deadline was highlighted by the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings.

Despite the move, on Wednesday, Minnesota head coach Kevin O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to Cousins as the starter this weekend against the Packers.

This could just be gamesmanship by O'Connell, but he told the media about Cousins starting: "I will say [we're] excited about the opportunity of spending every moment we can between now and then to get him comfortable and allow him to play for us this Sunday. That's what we're working towards, but also want to be fair to Kirk and make sure he feels good about it going to Lambeau Field."

Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said in his Wednesday press conference that he was surprised that the Raiders didn't get more for Cousins. "I was surprised [the Raiders] didn't get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for."

Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs may not end up on injured reserve despite needing surgery on his broken ring finger.

Jacobs, who is set to have that procedure later this week, could be back as soon as 2-3 weeks, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, who also reported that Green Bay will decide Saturday if IR is necessary.

The Packers play the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. But then they have a bye. There's a chance Jacobs returns for the following week's road game against the Los Angeles Rams.

The Chiefs will stick with Harrison Butker in Week 10, giving the kicker another chance to turn things around after weeks of struggles, head coach Andy Reid announced Wednesday.

After Sunday's win over the Jets, in which Butker missed another field goal attempt (a 51-yarder), Reid said that he would "look at everything" to assess whether it was time to move on. Evidently, Reid decided to stick with his long-time kicker.

Butker, who has spent his entire 10-year NFL career with the Chiefs, has seen his field goal accuracy crater this season. He's missed seven field goals in eight games so far this year, going 12-of-19 on attempts. That 63% completion rate is a noticeable dip from his previous decade of experience.

New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson will be back at practice Wednesday, albeit in a limited capacity while coming off a concussion, per ESPN's Rich Cimini.

Wilson was sidelined during last week's 35-12 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

He absorbed a blow to the head from safety Jeremy Chinn late in a Week 8 defeat to the Las Vegas Raiders. Wilson then reported concussion symptoms the following Monday, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters.

Wilson has piled up 43 receptions, 527 receiving yards and 3 receiving touchdowns this season.

The Cleveland Browns are expected to turn back to quarterback Deshaun Watson in Week 10, according to The Athletic.

The move was expected, as reports emerged Monday saying Watson would start for the team after clearing concussion protocol.

Browns head coach Todd Monken shot down those rumors Monday, however, saying he had yet to make a decision on the team's starter in Week 10.

With Watson sidelined, Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the 2026 season. He nearly led the Browns to an overtime win in that start.

Watson, who missed the contest due to a concussion, reportedly cleared league protocol Friday. Despite that, the was not active for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.

#2727. Hear Al Michaels' emotional tribute to Dan Hicks during 'Thursday Night Football'

The sports world mourns the passing of longtime broadcaster Dan Hicks, whose death was announced on Thursday, Nov. 12. He was 64 years old.

On "Thursday Night Football," Al Michaels shared some words about his friend's legacy on the Prime Video broadcast of the game between the New York Giants and Washington Commanders. He said he and his colleagues were "shocked" to hear the news that Hicks had passed away from what NBC Sports and Hicks' wife, Hannah Storm, said in a statement was an "acute illness."

Michaels reflected on Hicks' impressive resume across multiple sports. After Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992, Michaels said he "provided captions to so many iconic moments in golf, tennis and Notre Dame football. He and Rowdy Gaines turned the calling of swimming at multiple Olympics into an artform."

Michaels then turned to Hicks' character, remembering his kindness and joy.

"He was genial," he said. "He was compassionate, great company, had a world class sense of humor."

His voice broke as he sent his condolences to Storm and their children.

"On this very rough day for so many of us, we send our love to Hannah and your three daughters," Michaels said, choking up. "Wishing you strength and comfort."

Michaels' tribute was one of many that poured in after the news of Hicks' death broke. Leagues and fellow broadcasters posted heartfelt messages to honor their friend.

Gaines' reflection was especially saddening. The duo covered swimming for NBC for eight Olympics, beginning with the 1996 Summer Games in Atlanta. They called the 2008 Summer Games in Beijing, when the U.S. men's 4x100-meter freestyle relay swimming team, led by Michael Phelps, made one of the greatest comebacks in Olympic history to set a world record and take home the gold medal.

"My heart is broken," Gaines wrote on Instagram. "Danny wasn't just my partner in the booth for eight Olympics. He was one of my closest friends, someone I trusted with everything, both in and out of that arena. He was the glue that held us all together at all of those Games. He made me laugh like no other (person) ever has. We shared thousands of races and a friendship that went way beyond the pool deck. I'll miss his voice, his steadiness, and just having him next to me."

Hicks was scheduled to handle play-by-play duties for this weekend's Notre Dame game in South Bend, Indiana, in the battle between the Fighting Irish and Boston College.

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Hear Al Michaels' emotional tribute to Dan Hicks during 'Thursday Night Football'

#2726. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2724. Warriors ponder replacing injury-riddled Kristaps Porzingis with standout big men

It's no secret the Warriors need to acquire an impactful big man.

While it hasn't been a month since the NBA season started, Golden State appears to be aware of its deficiencies and is looking into fixing them.

According to NBA insider Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints, he's heard rumors of the Warriors being interested in Norman Powell but isn't buying into it. He mentioned two potential players.

Stephen Curry is out for at least two weeks, and the Warriors also need to find another big man. AP Photo/Ashley Landis

"Wendell Carter Jr. … from the Orlando Magic, a possible guy [they] could look to salary dump, to free up some cap space on their end," Siegel said.

"Then also, Naz Reid with the Charlotte Hornets. He was traded from the Minnesota Timberwolves to the Charlotte Hornets this past offseason," Siegel said. "Obviously he's had a ton of suitors between the Warriors, the Portland Trail Blazers. A few other teams mix out there."

As the Warriors are expected to search for a big man, the irony is that last season the organization thought it solved its problem when it made a splash at the trade deadline and acquired Kristaps Porzingis. Golden State gave him a two-year, $40 million contract extension over the offseason.

Yaxel Lendeborg celebrating during Sunday's game against the Rockets. Getty Images

Before this season began, Porzingis announced he would be out indefinitely due to a mystery illness.

Because Porzingis might never play in the NBA again, Golden State must pivot.

Last week, NBA insider Shams Charania reported the Warriors are not paying Porzingis because "he is not rendering services."

Kristaps Porzingis warming up for the Warriors last season in a game against the Kings. AP Photo/Scott Marshall

With a little more financial flexibility, Golden State could pull off a deal to get Carter. He is making $18.1 million this season and will make $19.6 million next season, while having a team option for the 2028-2029 season.

Reid is in the second year of a five-year, $125 million contract he originally signed with the Timberwolves.

Reid will make $23.3 million next year, $25 million the following, $26.7 million for 2028-2029 and has a player option of $28.4 million for the 2029-2030 season.

#2721. Orioles Predicted to Land Three-Time All-Star in Major Offseason Move

The Baltimore Orioles were one of the more frustrating teams in the baseball landscape this past season.

After a strong offseason, the Orioles couldn't do much with it, falling short of reaching the playoffs this year. The big move for Baltimore was signing slugger Pete Alonso, giving this team a legitimate offensive presence.

However, it wasn't enough for this group, and now the front office will be tasked with trying to get this team back to the playoffs. Many expect the Orioles to be active again this offseason, addressing some of the problems from the 2026 season.

One name that could be of interest for the Orioles is veteran outfielder Randy Arozarena, who will be a free agent. Arozarena isn't expected to return to the Seattle Mariners this offseason, opening the door for a team like Baltimore to strike.

MLB analyst Ryan Finkelstein of Just Baseball linked the Orioles with Arozarena, predicting the slugger will land in Baltimore. Arozarena is one of the better free agents on the market, and the Orioles could look to make another splash this offseason.

"From 2021 through 2025, Randy Arozarena averaged 22 home runs a season with a 122 wRC+. He was very consistent at being around 20-to-25% better than a league-average hitter by wRC+, while also adding value on the basepaths. Arozarena has reached the 20-20 club in each of his six full seasons in MLB.

That consistency alone would have gotten Arozarena paid, but to make his free agent case even better, Randy went out and posted the best season of his career in his walk year. By wRC+, Arozarena was the third-best qualified hitter in baseball, trailing only the two MVPs, Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong. With that platform year, Arozarena is a safe bet to be the highest-paid free agent bat on the market. Last offseason, the Baltimore Orioles ponied up and signed Pete Alonso on a five-year deal, and he immediately became their best player in 2026," Finkelstein wrote.

Arozarena was one of the few bright spots for the Mariners this past season, giving life to this offense during a down year. For the year, the slugger hit .281 with 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, and 26 stolen bases, while posting an OPS of .865.

Given where the Orioles are right now, the team does need to add more offense around Alonso, and Arozarena could bring the energy to this team. This was something that Baltimore was lacking last season, and Arozarena is one of the more fun players in the entire league.

While the Orioles could go after pitching this offseason, addressing the inconsistent offense does need to be done. Arozarena could be one of the bigger pieces added to this team, and he could be lethal in a lineup alongside Alonso and the others that Baltimore has.

Baltimore will have to open up the checkbook again to get a deal like this done, but it could be very worth it for this team. Overall, Arozarena feels like he could fit in well with the Orioles, helping them get back to the playoffs as early as next season.

#2719. NBA’s anti-tanking rules ironically tanking Utah Jazz season

I know that sports fans have said, "This is our year," at the beginning of every season for every sport since the dawn of man. Archaeologists only recently discovered cave drawings of ancient man calling his shot by prematurely tattooing the Larry O'Brien Trophy on his shoulder with the description: "Tigris River Valley Hunter-Gatherers 5,000 B.C. World Champions" (no need to fact-check me on this, just trust me).

But for the Utah Jazz, the 2026-27 season was actually supposed to be "their year". No blind optimism, no baseless fantasies. Just grounded, reasonable, and logical projections for a team on the rise.

Through four painful seasons, the Jazz lost a grand total of 211 games in search of an elusive young superstar to lift their tragic franchise from an endless tank. As those four seasons came to a close, Utah finally claimed their prize: a star guard out of Kansas named Darryn Peterson. And he couldn't have come at a better time, either.

Tired of witnessing one-third of the league actively trying to lose basketball games, the NBA enacted anti-tanking protocols and installed lottery reform intent on de-incentivizing the act of "tanking".

Teams have far less incentive to tank this season, especially this early on, as the owners of the four worst records will have a statistically lower chance of getting the number-one overall pick than those who finish 5th-8th from the bottom.

That adjustment is one of two reasons why Utah is off to such a slow start. The other, in my view, is having a very injured roster at a time when most teams are still playing at or near full strength. Teams are fighting to win every game, and the Jazz are ill-equipped to fight back.

As a result, the Jazz are off to an even worse start this year through 11 games than any of their rebuilding seasons. They hold hands at the bottom of the Western Conference standings with an abysmal Sacramento team.

2022-23: 8-32023-24: 4-72024-25: 3-82025-26: 4-72026-27: 1-11

The Jazz are not tanking. Not intentionally, anyway.

Utah has even less reason to minimize their competitive edge, being barred from a top-four pick after drafting second overall this summer, and owing their pick to Memphis even if it were to finish in a favorable position.

With three of their five starters out with prolonged injuries, things may get even worse before they get any better. But they can — and I believe Utah will — improve before a play-in spot is out of reach.

Assuming Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic all return according to current timetables, the Jazz are only a month or two away from full strength, barring further injury. This is a team still learning to play with each other. With several key pieces having arrived within the last year, chemistry will take time to develop.

A Play-In appearance is a reasonable goal this season, despite my own preseason projections anticipating a top-six finish. Should the Jazz rally and finish with a top-10 record in the Western Conference, Utah has hope of building on that success in the following season. This was never going to be "the year" for Utah. It was always destined to be a stepping stone. But so long as that stride carries the Jazz closer to a better place, there's still reason for optimism.

This is a talented team. Time will tell if talent can translate to results.

Calvin Barrett is the Associate Editor for SLC Dunk and a Utah Jazz columnist for the Standard-Examiner. Originally from Springville, Utah, he currently writes from his desk in Japan.

#2717. Marcus Smart suspended for throwing punch that made contact with Warriors player's face

Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart has been suspended for "throwing a punch that made contact with the face" of opponent Charles Bassey during Wednesday's game against the Golden State Warriors.

The NBA released a statement on Thursday, Nov. 12 announcing the Rockets guard is being suspended three games without pay for the incident.

The night before, Smart grazed the face of Bassey when he threw a punch with 21 seconds left in the third quarter after the whistle was blown for a separate foul. Their arms had been caught in each other during a play and, when game play was stopped, Smart seemingly snapped.

After the punch was thrown, players from both teams got in a scuffle and, as the scene was broken up, the 2021-22 Defensive Player of the Year started walking to the locker room. It seemed as if he was sure he would be given a flagrant foul 2 and ejected from the game, which, after a review, he was.

Just before the incident, Smart and Bassey got tangled up under the rim when trying to box out during a Warriors possession. The two continued to jaw at each other up the floor. Then, when play halted, Smart squared up and threw a right-handed hook that nearly landed on Bassey's cheek. Bassey had moved his head backward to avoid contact. Officials later said that Smart made contact to Bassey's nose.

After the game, which the Rockets won 115-108, Bassey criticized Smart for his "fake toughness."

Houston head coach Ime Udoka also addressed the incident and shared Smart's side of the story.

"Marcus, I just talked to him, he said they got wrapped up and his elbow that he had hurt got bent up," the coach said. "And so he said something to him and Bassey said, 'What you going to do?' and he did it."

The former Oklahoma State standout will miss the Rockets' next three games due to his suspension. Houston faces the Utah Jazz, Washington Wizards and Miami Heat.

Smart's suspension will be lifted to play in the road game against the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

Smart is averaging 8.3 points, 2.6 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal per game this season, his first with the Rockets.

He had six points, two rebounds and an assist before being booted from the Warriors matchup.

#2716. Cunningham's incredible night — 52 points, 11 assists, no turnovers — saves Pistons in double OT

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Washington Wizards kept making last-second shots, forcing Cade Cunningham to play an extra 10 minutes.

All that did was turn a great night into a historic one for the Detroit star.

Cunningham scored 52 points and had 11 assists, leading the Pistons to a 144-140 win in double overtime Thursday night. He became the first player since at least 1978 with at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game with no turnovers. In a game that was tight pretty much throughout, Cunningham kept mistakes to a minimum while still being incredibly productive.

"It was the best I've ever done it in my NBA career for sure," Cunningham said.

Cunningham had only 22 points after three quarters before scoring 18 in the fourth. That still wasn't enough because Trae Young's 3-pointer at the buzzer tied the game at 121. Then Washington scored the first seven points of overtime, but there was still plenty of time for Cunningham. A jumper, two free throws and a 3-pointer later, he'd tied the game at 130.

Duncan Robinson put the Pistons ahead with a jumper, but AJ Dybantsa — the top overall pick in this year's draft — tied it with less than a second left for Washington.

There were four players in this game who were picked No. 1 overall — Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, Deandre Ayton and Cunningham. Davis had 30 points and 15 rebounds for the Wizards before fouling out in the second overtime after Cunningham made a 3 to put the Pistons up 135-132.

Young scored 37 points and Alex Sarr added 30. The Wizards had not had three 30-point scorers in a game since Nov. 18, 1969, when the team was called the Baltimore Bullets and Mike Davis, Earl Monroe and Gus Johnson formed the high-scoring trio against the San Diego Rockets.

Cunningham equaled the fourth-highest scoring total in franchise history for the Pistons. Jerry Stackhouse scored 57 points in a 2001 game, Kelly Tripucka had 56 in 1983, Dave Bing had 54 in 1971 and George Yardley scored 52 in 1958.

No other Detroit player scored more points than Daniss Jenkins' 21, and he didn't have any after the third quarter. Down the stretch, Cunningham took over, even overshadowing teammate Ausar Thompson's first career triple-double.

"He led us through the fourth quarter and overtimes," said Thompson, who had 17 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds. "He did what he does. One person can't just guard him."

#2714. Sixers take care of business without LeBron, secure 10th vs. Raptors

Maybe not the blowout people are looking for, but still a pretty decent win. The Sixers erased a 17-point first half deficit to defeat the Toronto Raptors 123-112 Thursday night.

Tyrese Maxey led the Sixers with 27 shooting 8-of-13 from the field along with eight assists. Joel Embiid didn't quite break out of his shooting slump, but looked much better as he avoided an injury scare early in the game. He finished with 20 points going 7-of-17 from the floor along with four rebounds.

Jaylen Brown had an up-and-down night, going 8-of-15 from the field for 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe had another great swiss army knife game, finishing with 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. R.J. Barrett led all scorers with 31.

LeBron James was out for this one with lower back management, as well as Adem Bona (neck) and Dominick Barlow (back). Toronto was without Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes, and Trayce Jackson-Davis.

The Sixers opened the game generating good shots. Brown shook free of CMB for a pull-up jumper, Dean Wade and Edgecombe both stepped into open threes, and Embiid got a jumper from the free throw line, but none of these looks fell. Maxey finally got the Sixers their first field goal of the game getting the ball off a broken play and getting to the basket.

Embiid set a screen for Maxey to help him get open on the three-point line and appeared to bang knees with Ja'Kobe Walter as Walter was trying to fight through the screen. Embiid went down in a heap of pain immediately and the Sixers stopped the game so he could head back to the locker room.

The Sixers' offense continued to struggle after the stoppage. Brown was trying attack off the dribble but was getting bottled up. They still couldn't hit a three off the catch either — the rest of the team started the game 0-of-4 from deep. The Raptors ripped off a 12-0 run during this stretch.

For the second game in a row, Edgecombe had a really nice spin move to split defenders and get to the basket. Darko Rajakovich called timeout after he did so, which allowed Embiid to emerge from the locker room and return to the game. Edgecombe did just about the same thing coming out of the timeout.

Maxey ran quick off a miss to create a fast break layup, but Toronto was able to snuff out the momentum quickly. The Sixers went into a zone for a couple of possessions, but the Raptors shooters had gotten into a rhythm and they were able to get open pretty easily. Two threes from Barrett and another from Jamison Battle helped them score 13 more unanswered points.

Embiid nearly passed up a wide open layup near the basket, but did eventually put it up once he realized the 6-foot-1 Jamal Shead was guarding him for his first field goal of the game. Maxey was able to hit a ridiculous layup in transition, and Anfernee Simons drilled a three at the buzzer to pull the Sixers to within nine.

Simons drilled a stepback three with a hand in his face to open the quarter. Embiid, looking a bit more comfortable, blocked a layup and got himself an easy bucket going to the paint. Brown wasn't able to bury his three after making Kyle Anderson fall with a crossover, but he finally got a midrange to go that capped off a 15-0 Sixers run going back to the first.

That seemed to do the trick as Brown drilled his next two pull-ups in the midrange. Edgecombe was the best Sixer on the floor for much of the first half. His intercepting of passes from the weak side was the best defense they had going for them, and it was creating plenty of transition opportunities. On top of a big fast break dunk, Edgecombe also hit a very nifty up-and-under layup.

It probably gave everyone a good scare, but Embiid was able to get by Jakob Poeltl and throw down a dunk, albeit one that did not look like the smoothest landing. The Sixers' offense started scorching, but a lack of stops prevented them from building a lead. Nick Nurse called a timeout to regroup after they allowed two offensive rebounds on one possession, ending with a putback.

That timeout also gave Nurse a chance to put Maxey back in the game, who immediately went straight to the basket and got fouled. After teams traded threes, Maxey got to the hoop again, but Embiid picked up his third foul of the night trying to grab a defensive rebound and had to sit for the last two and a half minutes of the half.

Brown took up the mantle offensively, nailing another pull-up and driving for a layup. Jabari Walker, who didn't have much of an impact in his first shift, picked up an offensive rebound and drew a foul pulling down another. His putback was answered with another three from Barrett. Wade missed another open three on the ensuing possession, keeping the game tied at 60 at the break.

Both teams stayed hot coming out of the break as Wade and Edgecombe each drilled a corner three. On the other end of the floor the Raptors drove right to the basket for three easy layups. Immanuel Quickley also drilled a very deep, very contested pull-up three. Embiid missed a fadeaway over Poeltl, but got himself another easy dunk playing high-low with Edgecombe.

The Sixers were still giving up plenty of easy baskets off simple actions, but they were guarding one-on-one better when the Raptors isolated. Brown blocked a Barrett layup and jumped a passing lane for a pick-six. Screens ended up being risky plays on the night as Kentavious Caldwell-Pope came up favoring his shoulder trying to fight through one, but he didn't have to leave the game.

Despite throwing a post-entry pass for Brown a little too far, Embiid seemed to finding his comfort offensively. He was confident in his physical advantages over Poeltl and was aggressive because of that. It did seem like he was trying to dunk as much as he could, which did lead to him fumbling away an attempt at the basket.

Embiid is still waiting on that midrange game to come back around as he was long on another free throw line jumper. It remained a hot Simons game, something the team desperately needed with how they've been shooting lately.

Maxey was a consistent source of scoring to close the quarter, but stops on the other end continued to come at a premium. The Sixers were finally able to get some space after Quickley missed a pretty open layup after beating Maxey through the paint. Simons got it up the floor for a transition basket. The Raptors called a timeout to regroup, but CMB got called for a moving screen on the first play coming out of it. Maxey got to the line, which Barrett responded to by backing him down in the post for a layup, bringing the Sixers lead back down to nine after three.

Walker opened the quarter with a corner three and just missed a second a few possessions later. He did scoop up another putback after Edgecombe's attempt to dunk on two Raptors came up empty, and Simons swiped the ball away from Barrett for a fast break bucket to start the quarter strong.

At some point in the first half, the ball got stuck behind the backboard and the crowd let Poeltl hear it as he struggled to knock it free with a broom. When the ball got stuck again in the fourth, a referee brought the broom back to Poeltl on the bench for a chance at redemption. The crowd got a kick out of it, but Poeltl did not, and refused. The crowd shared a sarcastic celebration with KCP after it took him a few attempts to dislodge it.

The Sixers' offense seemed to hit a bit of a lull midway through the fourth. Brown missed a pair of free throws and was blocked again at the rim by CMB. Edgecombe tried to hit Brown with a lob but that was broken up by CMB again, but Edgecombe was able to pick it back up and finish it himself. After giving up second chance points on the following possession, Nurse called a timeout to put Embiid and Maxey back in the game.

The Raptors got another basket inside, a trip to the line, and a corner three to cut the lead down to six with plenty of time left. Simons hit a much needed three, as was the case for much of the night. Embiid finally knocked down a midrange after a couple of stops, but Quickley walked into an open three off a screen on the next trip down the floor.

Maxey got to the line again as the Raptors started to run out of time. Embiid got past a couple of defenders and nearly had another self lob off the backboard, but that was also broken up by CMB. Embiid was still able to secure the ball and get it to KCP, who buried a three right before the shot clock expired. Embiid hit a midrange on the following possession, wrapping up this game quite nicely for both himself and the team.

The double-digit lead gave the fans enough confidence for loud "We Want Tacko" chants, and Nurse obliged, putting Tacko Fall in for the final 54 seconds of the game. Poor Jabari Walker got a round of boos when he went to the scorer's table on account of not being Tacko Fall.

#2709. AFC North Week 9 Recap: Joe Burrow strengthens MVP bid

The AFC North standings did not change in Week 9, with only one team getting a win.

The Steelers enjoyed their bye week at the top of the division. Pittsburgh will now have to defend first place when they return to action in Week 10 against the Bengals.

Cincinnati moved to 6-2 with a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain.

Joe Burrow has firmly planted himself in the MVP race following another strong performance. Against the Falcons, Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns while adding another touchdown on the ground. Over his last four games, Burrow has accounted for 18 touchdowns. Ja'Marr Chase was Burrow's leading receiver against Atlanta with 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown, while Tee Higgins had a pair of touchdowns to go with 32 yards on five catches.

The Bengals defense did not record a sack on quarterback Michael Penix, but the unit did enough to hold the Falcons' talented offense in check. Barrett Carter had the lone turnover of the game with an interception off Penix. Cincinnati will have the opportunity to challenge for the division lead now in Week 10.

The Browns dropped their second consecutive game with a 23-22 loss to the New Orleans Saints.

Shedeur Sanders got the start at quarterback in place of the injured Deshaun Watson in Week 9. Sanders finished the game 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, with another 28 yards on 10 carries. Denzel Boston's 98 receiving yards on six catches led the offense, while KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. were the recipients of Sanders' touchdowns. Fannin's touchdown was particularly impressive as he broke multiple tackles on his way to a 39-yard score in overtime. Cleveland went for the win with a two-point attempt, but Sanders was unable to connect with Boston on the play.

The Browns' defense racked up five sacks on Tyler Shough, with Carson Schwesinger and Myles Harden both finishing with two. Schwesinger had 15 total tackles while also forcing a fumble to go with his pair of sacks.

The Ravens lost their fourth game in a row with a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football.

Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano started the game at quarterback on a short week after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley were injured in the previous game. Fagnano struggled as you would expect, completing 10 of 18 pass attempts for just 60 yards and a pair of interceptions. Justice Hill was the leading rusher with nine carries for 85 yards and a touchdown, with most of the work coming on a 65-yard score in the fourth quarter. Baltimore has since acquired veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, whom they hope can keep their season alive for a potential Jackson return down the road.

The Ravens' defense had a tough hill to climb with little to no help from their own offense, but the unit was supposed to be a strength of the team heading into the season. Instead, Baltimore's defense has allowed over 30 points in three straight games.

#2708. Harry Kane marks historic 126th England cap with a little reminder of his greatness

Harry Kane was asked this week to name the lowest moment of his 125 England caps, and his mind travelled back to that evening in Qatar when he sent a penalty over Hugo Lloris's crossbar and up to the heavens. Kane being Kane, he would score the next 30 penalties of his career. "It made me improve," he said. "A lot of the bad things have helped me get to where I am now."

Perhaps it was apt, then, that on the night of his record-breaking 126th England cap, Kane scored his 92nd England goal from the penalty spot to settle this 2-1 win over Croatia and book a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals. It was a little display of his work ethic, a simple kick of the ball honed to a fine point through thousands of repetitions on the training ground.

Kane dinked his penalty down the middle and a diving Dominik Livakovic almost blocked the ball with his trail leg. The goalkeeper beat the ground in frustration as if to say, I knew you'd do that. But perhaps this is the point: since that World Cup miss against France, Kane has trained every penalty into his armoury – the stutter or the run, the blast or the dink, left or right or the space a goalkeeper leaves behind – and Livakovic couldn't cover them all.

It came after a rare miss for Bayern Munich last month. "The next one is always important to bounce back," Kane said. "I did my usual routine yesterday in training and looked at the goalkeeper. I haven't gone down the middle with a penalty for maybe three or four years. With penalties, you have to keep things fresh, keep things moving. I thought it was a good time to do it, looking at his clips. Thankfully, it paid off today."

Kane's penalty evades the leg of Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic (PA)

What did we learn from this slightly underwhelming performance? England are better than Croatia, but then we saw that at the World Cup when England beat them 4-2, and more emphatically in Rijeka last month when England won 7-0. This was naturally a more cautious Croatia, against an altogether sloppier England who made a series of uncharacteristic errors all over the field.

Trent Alexander-Arnold gave the ball away on the edge of his own box, Lewis Hall played a fancy flick straight off the pitch and Jarell Quansah assisted Croatia's equaliser with a deft, daft header inside his own six-yard box. Jude Bellingham showed frustration towards some of his teammates' errors, yet his best game largely deserted him too.

The England fans who shivered through these 90 minutes might instead remember the few moments beforehand. The commemorations began with a giant Tifo behind one goal displaying England's captain roaring into the night sky with the words "England's finest" and "Kane 126" emblazoned top and bottom. Kane emerged from the tunnel with his four children as mascots, and then spent a couple of minutes waving around the Ballon d'Or before being presented with three gifts, like a scene from the nativity. The three wise men were played by Peter Shilton (gift one: a golden crest), Croatia captain Luka Modric (gift two: an old football), and Prince William (gift three: a framed shirt).

"It's been a crazy few weeks," Kane said. "It takes a lot out of you emotionally, physically and mentally ... it's a hard balance because you want to take it in. Breaking the record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo there, having my kids with me, and being presented by all the people was beyond dreams, so of course you have got to take it in. Once the whistle goes and you're on the pitch, you just start focusing on what your job is."

Kane poses with Prince Phillip and Peter Shilton (Reuters)

England started haphazardly but began to get a grip midway through the first half and it was Kane who unlocked Croatia's defence with a raking pass to Bellingham arriving at the far post. Bellingham's first-time cross found Morgan Rogers, who managed to impart just enough energy to the ball to bounce it home from three yards.

Kane had to wait. His first big chance came early in the second half when he received a cutback in the box from Declan Rice and a half-empty goal prepared to bulge, but Josip Stanisic wasn't feeling sentimental and he lunged in front to block Kane's goalbound shot.

Croatia drew level a few minutes later when Quansah took the extraordinary step of attempting a header back to Jordan Pickford inside a crowded penalty area. Pickford understandably wasn't expecting the pass, and he was beaten to the ball by Petar Sucic who knocked it into the roof of England's goal.

But Quansah went some way to making amends when his run drew some suspicious shirt pulling from Ivan Smolcic. Danish referee Morten Krogh missed it at first look but VAR intervened, and when Kane placed the ball down on the spot, the rest felt inevitable.

Kane celebrates after scoring from the spot (PA)

England now travel to Madrid to face Spain on Sunday, where victory would clinch top spot in the group. It would also serve as a sign of England's standing in the game right now if they were to beat the world champions on their own turf, after a narrow but encouraging 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in September.

Kane will earn cap number 127 and he is intent on gathering many more. Since winning the Ballon d'Or he has made his remaining career targets abundantly clear: scoring 100 England goals, winning the Champions League with Bayern Munich and winning a major trophy for England.

Whether the Nations League counts as "major" is debatable – Cristiano Ronaldo might say yes but just about everyone else says no – yet it presents an opportunity to end England's 60-year wait for a men's trophy. It would be fitting if Kane, now England's greatest player by any measure, was the man to lift it.

Marc Cucurella has been booed by German fans ever since Euro 2024, when he controversially blocked a shot from Jamal Musiala with his arm inside the penalty area.

The referee decided against awarding Germany a penalty, and Spain went on to win the quarter-final 2-1 after extra time thanks to Mikel Merino's late winner.

“Yes, yes, yes, without a doubt. But I don't know why they've taken it out on me. Well, that's how it is.

“I know I can't play in Germany. I'm very much loved there,” he added with a laugh.

#2706. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2705. Thursday Night Football: Commanders lead Giants 10-7 at halftime

The Giants and Commanders played a first half fitting the weather. On a cold, rainy night, the Commanders lead the Giants 10-7 at halftime.

Ben Sinnott caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Jayden Daniels with 5 seconds remaining in the first half. It completed a nine-play, 67-yard drive.

Washington also had an 11-play, 49-yard drive that ended with Drew Stevens' 46-yard field goal.

#2704. Defense must show for Bengals to win AFC North showdown with Steelers

There's no getting around it: This edition of the Cincinnati Bengals versus Pittsburgh Steelers is a truly big game.

It's November, it's chilly and getting colder, and the top spot in the AFC North will be on the line Nov. 15 when the Bengals and Steelers meet at Paycor Stadium for an 8:20 p.m. Sunday Night Football game. It's cliche, but this is what it's all about.

Based on what the teams have on their respective schedules in the months to come, the winner of the Nov. 15 clash could have a significant leg-up in determining the AFC North champion. It's a must-win for both clubs no matter how you look at it.

Bengals trade deadline Zac Taylor Bengals take accountability for failed trade attempt with Eagles

Here are some considerations and must-haves for the Bengals if they're to emerge atop the AFC North following this game:

Sure, Cincinnati would love to have its defense create chaos for 60 minutes against the Steelers. Negative-yardage plays. Turnovers. Making Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers uncomfortable all night. The Bengals are more than welcome to do all of that against the Steelers − but it won't take 60 minutes of perfection to get the win Cincinnati needs.

The Bengals defense has its issues. Missed tackles and a tendency to allow explosive plays are chief among them. Teams have racked up big yardage totals against the Bengals, too. But the bottom line is what opponents convert into actual points, and Cincinnati's 21.9 opponent points per game, which ranks No. 14 in the NFL, is solid.

Cincinnati has held opposing offenses to 20 points or less three times this season, and that sets the team's explosive offense up nicely to out-gun almost any team in the NFL. And bear in mind that while the Steelers are one of two teams to put up 30 points on the defense this year, Pittsburgh is far from the most prolific offense in the league. Give Pittsburgh full marks for its 6-2 start, but the offense's 22.9 points per game is ranked just the No. 17 unit in the NFL. That's a number the Bengals offense can more than keep up with if the defense can set the table.

If the Bengals' defense can just get off the field in key spots and generally be what it's been all season, that'll be "mission accomplished" for coordinator Al Golden's unit.

When divisional opponents meet for the second time in an NFL season, those games are often framed within the context of the last time the teams met. Sometimes, that's fair to do, but not in this case. If you're the Bengals, keep these facts in mind about the Sept. 27 loss at Acrisure Stadium because a lot has changed in the 49 days between that game and Nov. 15

The Bengals' offensive line is playing at a higher level than it was Sept. 27. It's been a while since quarterback Joe Burrow was getting knocked around like he was in September (and don't forget the Steelers clinched their Sept. 27 win with a sack and a fumble recovery late in regulation).

Burrow has grown into the 2026 season and is now playing some of the best football of his career. Back in Week 3, the talk around Burrow was about a slower start to his year than expected. Today? He's leading the NFL with 23 touchdown passes and a 74% completion percentage, and is No. 2 in passing yards with 2,386 yards.

Since the Bengals are coming off a win in Madrid, there's also been considerable talk about the 0-5 record of NFL teams coming off an international game when playing a team coming off a bye. And the stat makes sense: There's no question about which team would be more rested, but these matchups are a relatively new thing (hence there are only five prior examples). In the past, playing abroad meant going straight into your bye, but that appears to be a bygone luxury for teams and schedule-makers. For the Bengals, it's not quantum physics or higher math, though. They can figure out how to do this and become the first team in this situation to win coming off playing abroad. The team has eased back into preparations for Pittsburgh with great care. For instance, Wednesday's practice inside Paycor Stadium was a walk-through as players continued to reacclimatize.

Basically, the Sept. 27 game isn't so relevant this week. Neither is that 0-5 record, which has nothing whatsoever to do with the Bengals. These subjects are just noise, and Cincinnati needs to block them out.

The 2026 Bengals were invested in heavily by the front office for games exactly like this one. Dexter Lawrence II, Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen? And don't forget the Burrow-Ja'Marr Chase-Tee Higgins triumvirate. All of these players (and their price tags) were assembled to win these high-stakes games.

Since the spring, all the talk has been about the Bengals contending for an AFC North title, and more. Well, that means this team's stars have to show up, lead, and deliver. Not next week against the Commanders, and certainly in two weeks when the national TV cameras are far from Paycor Stadium when the New Orleans Saints come to town.

Based on the number of remaining games, the math suggests the Bengals could go 0-2 against Pittsburgh and still accomplish all their goals. Reality, and the makeup of those remaining games, indicates there's far less math to suggest Cincinnati can win the North by going winless against the Steelers.

It's been years since Cincinnati had a game like this in its backyard. Burrow lobbied for the pieces that could allow the organization to be successful on nights like this. It's time to go.

Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart has been suspended by the NBA for three games after an attempted punch against Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

And don't forget the Burrow-Ja'Marr Chase-Tee Higgins triumvirate. All of these players (and their price tags) were assembled to win these high-stakes games.

Since the spring, all the talk has been about the Bengals contending for an AFC North title, and more. Well, that means this team's stars have to show up, lead, and deliver. Not next week against the Commanders, and certainly in two weeks when the national TV cameras are far from Paycor Stadium when the New Orleans Saints come to town.

Based on the number of remaining games, the math suggests the Bengals could go 0-2 against Pittsburgh and still accomplish all their goals. Reality, and the makeup of those remaining games, indicates there's far less math to suggest Cincinnati can win the North by going winless against the Steelers.

It's been years since Cincinnati had a game like this in its backyard. Burrow lobbied for the pieces that could allow the organization to be successful on nights like this. It's time to go.

#2700. Toronto falls to stacked Sixers’ offence

The Toronto Raptors continued a challenging stretch of their schedule tonight, facing the Philadelphia 76ers on the second night of a back-to-back, this time on the road. After coming apart at the seams despite an early lead against Boston, the Raptors' intention to move on was thwarted by a Sixers team that handed the Raptors a similar loss. A significant early lead dwindled by the half, ultimately leading to Toronto falling, this time 112 to 123.

To no surprise, Philly's big names of Joel Embiid (20 points), Jaylen Brown (18 points), VJ Edgecombe (15 points), and TJ Maxey (27 points) carried the Sixers. Anfernee Simons was their most productive bench player, offering clutch long-range shooting that gave the rest of the team space to operate, finishing with 17 points in the process.

Toronto saw excellent performances from RJ Barrett who finished with 31 points, 14 rebounds, and 5 assists, Immanuel Quickley who had 26 points, 4 rebounds, and 6 assists, and Collin Murray-Boyles chipping in 14 points, 4 assists, and 5 blocks.

The Raptors had their hands full early, needing to answer for a number of offensive weapons on a Sixers team that is building plenty of hype for a championship contender. They didn't need to face LeBron James who sat due to sciatica, but the remaining four of their starters remained a formidable challenge.

Toronto targeted Embiid early, forcing him into awkward defensive coverages that required speed and lateral movement that he struggled with as a result of his laundry list of injuries. After knee-to-knee contact, Embiid briefly visited the locker room but returned a few minutes later.

RJ and Quickley were quick to answer their less-than-savory performances last night. Quickley worked hard to distribute the ball and get everyone going early while RJ hit a pair of threes on consecutive possessions.

Just like last night, their offense was running smoothly. They built a significant 33-16 lead, and it felt like everything was going in the Raptors' favour until in the final two minutes of the frame, the tide slowly started to turn. Philly went on an unanswered 8-point run to close the quarter.

In the second quarter, the Sixers were able to close the gap and draw ahead, making much of the second frame a back-and-forth contest.

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons showed their abilities from beyond the arc, creating spacing for the Sixers' starters to operate in the paint where they're comfortable. Tyrese Maxey was almost unstoppable from virtually everywhere on the floor. Jaylen Brown started to come alive as well, an equally challenging offensive player to find an answer for.

Toronto had contributions from everyone, with CMB, Barrett, Martin, and Battle all making long range shots. Their ball movement helped limit poor shot selection, and even when they were missing shots, Walter stood out as having a motor, with a phenomenal put-back that showed the Raptors were going to fight through the fatigue. By the end of the half, the game was all tied up.

The third quarter mirrored the second, going blow-for-blow with Philly. Ties and lead changes riddled the period, with neither team able to build any kind of momentum or separation.

Alijah Martin has impressed with his continued active defence and fearless scoring, willing to take the ball through anyone. At times, the minutes with mostly bench players on the floor actually felt more cohesive and productive than without.

Despite best efforts, Philly's top four firepower was hard to contend with. Late in the third, a series of costly turnovers allowed the Sixers to get out in transition, managing a 8-0 run to build their largest lead, a 9-point advantage before the final twelve minutes of play.

Toronto's fatigue might have played a role as this game started to get away from them. Second effort isn't enough when you're struggling to make second and third shots, and despite their effort, a lot of them rolled off the rim and couldn't be recovered. Murray-Boyles' effort, however, should be celebrated. On one end, he was blocking shots and playing tough defence, and on the other, good screening and off-ball movement helped him be a standout on the court.

In the end, it wasn't enough to overcome Philly, and Toronto continues to seek their first win against a team over 0.500. Next, they'll face New York twice, with the first of the matchups on Sunday at 6 pm.

#2698. JJ Redick on why he reinserted Luka Doncic late in Wednesday's game

For the Los Angeles Lakers, Luka Doncic normally rests during the first several minutes of the second and fourth quarters of games. When they entered the fourth quarter of Wednesday's game against the Milwaukee Bucks, they held a 94-73 lead, and with 6:51 remaining, they were still up by 20 points.

That is when Luka Doncic came back into the game, which was surely something that had fans wondering whether it was a wise decision. Sure enough, a little later, he landed on Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma while making a long jumper and tweaked his right ankle, forcing him to exit the game almost immediately.

Typically, coaches are reluctant to put their stars and starters back in a game deep into the fourth quarter when their team has a big lead in order to avoid injuries. Lakers coach JJ Redick was asked after Wednesday's game why he reinserted Doncic despite being in full control, via Lakers Nation.

"We decided, because of how that Raptors game went, we said alright, four minutes, 20 points, somewhere around there that's kind of the cutoff point. I don't think Luka would have gotten back in the game had Collin [Sexton] not busted his head open. So not having Collin, not having AR (Austin Reaves), you put Luka back in, you're playing for two minutes. He's gonna either keep the lead or build the lead and then he tweaks his ankle. There's nothing you can do about that."

Reaves, of course, had to leave the game in the third quarter due to a heel ailment he sustained on a dunk. Then midway through the fourth quarter, Sexton suffered an open wound on his head after a head-to-head collision with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins. Sexton required sutures to close the resulting wound, according to Redick.

The good news is that Doncic may be OK for the Lakers' next game, which won't be until Sunday and will take place against the Phoenix Suns. Shams Charania of ESPN reported on Thursday that Doncic woke up without pain in the right ankle he tweaked.

Even without Doncic, Reaves and Sexton, the Lakers finished off the Bucks for a 123-112 victory that gave them an 11-2 record and a seven-game winning streak. That 11-2 mark is the best record in the NBA.

#2696. Cade Cunningham has historic night as Pistons outlast Wizards in bloody battle

AJ Dybantsa collided with Cade Cunningham during the Washington Wizards' game against the Detroit Pistons on Thursday, Nov. 12 and was bloodied on the play.

Dybantsa didn't miss any action and even sent the game into its second overtime, but Cunningham ended up being the star of the game. The Pistons guard scored a career-high 52 points at Capital One Arena to dismantle the Wizards 144-140 in double overtime. He added 11 assists, five rebounds, a steal and a block. He did not commit a turnover.

According to the league, he is the first player ever to notch at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game without turning the ball over.

The 2021 No. 1 overall pick passed his previous career high when he scored his 47th point in the first overtime with a 3-point bucket that tied the game at 130.

As for the collision, with 26 seconds left in regulation and the Wizards up 118-117, Cunningham was dribbling the ball and attempted to twirl and switch directions. The Wizards rookie and 2026 No. 1 overall pick was guarding him and, when Cunningham spun back around, his jaw smacked into the side of Dybantsa's face.

Dybantsa fell backwards onto the court and grabbed his mouth as he laid on his back. Blood started dripping from his mouth. A trainer tended to him as he continued lying on the hardwood.

The game went into overtime with the score tied at 121 at the end of the fourth quarter. Dybantsa sent the game to a second overtime, seemingly no worse for wear. He took a pass from Trae Young, dribbled and took a jump shot at the charity stripe to tie the game at 132 with 0.1 second left.

The rookie finished with five points, eight rebounds and four assists for the Wizards.

Washington was led by Young, who had 37 points and 14 assists. Anthony Davis notched a double-double of his own with 30 points and 15 boards. Alex Sarr added 30 points and nine rebounds.

Warburton, from Colwyn Bay, believes he has earned this career-defining shot after years of overcoming the odds on the British scene.

"You're in there to do a job. Yes, he's a world champion, but this is my time to show the world that I belong at this level," Warburton told BBC Sport.

"All of my hard work has got me here. This is a big hurdle to get over, but I've been jumping over hurdles my whole career."

The 5ft 11in (1.8m) former Welsh middleweight champion added: "This is another occasion to prove wrong those people who think I can't achieve something. I don't feel any pressure - the pressure is all on him.

"He's the WBC champion. He's the one who has set out to put on a show-stopping performance as world champ. I'm going there to upset the apple cart."

Workaholic with a tattooed throat – meet The Merthyr Mexican

Price rules out Shields but hints at big showdown

Headlining Zuffa Boxing's first show in Saudi Arabia will mark a new high point in a "crazy" rise for Warburton, who never set out to become a world champion.

He faces a quick turnaround, too, having beaten veteran Englishman Nathan Heaney to retain his WBA continental middleweight title on 26 September.

Consecutive victories over former British champion Heaney have given Warburton's career fresh momentum, exceeding even his own expectations.

"I never thought that beating Nathan Heaney twice would have gotten me where I am now. I took the risk to face him twice, and it's brought a reward," Warburton said.

Initially, Warburton had his eyes on the Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury undercard in Cardiff before landing a fight that he thought was a joke when first informed.

"I was back in the gym training full time and had a phone call from my manager telling me they had asked Zuffa if I could face a certain boxer," Warburton recalled.

"They came back and said no, but that I could face Carlos Adames. I was taken aback and thought, 'Are you telling me lies? Is this true?'

"After a split second, it hit me that I had finally got a good reward for all of my hard work, and then he dropped the news that it wouldn't be for his WBC title.

"As they say in boxing, things happen quickly. Beat Carlos Adames and I could be on the road for the WBC world title."

Gerome Warburton beat Nathan Heaney for the WBA continental middleweight title in March [Getty Images]

Wales has a rich history of world champion boxers, but none of the 14 men and women who have claimed top honours in the sport hail from north Wales.

Barmouth-born Johnny Williams held the British and Empire heavyweight titles, but he received his boxing education after moving to English town Rugby at age three.

Warburton now has the chance to become north Wales' most celebrated boxer, as he prepares to become the first from the region to face a world champion.

"I feel as though I don't get the recognition for doing that," he added.

"I'm holding the flag for north Wales. If I could get my hands on a world title, or box for one, it would be a dream come true, and I'd be writing history."

Warburton, who goes by the moniker 'The Breadmaker', will not be joined by family for the trip to Saudi Arabia, but knows they will be watching back home.

While son Roman was present for both fights against Heaney and celebrated in the ring, Warburton prefers to "zone in" when fighting further afield.

"Unfortunately, I've banned all of my family members from going over because I treat boxing like work," Warburton explained.

"My family come when I fight closer to home, but when I'm away, I like to be on my own with my team. They wouldn't come to work with me.

"I have to be zoned in, and I know that everyone will be watching from home. One of my friends is coming because he likes to be adventurous."

Warburton expects the Riyadh crowd to be behind Adames and believes that will play into his hands, as it has done throughout his career.

"I'm used to not having the crowd [behind me] and having them boo me. The two Heaney fights showed that," he said.

"I could go into the lion's den, and it still wouldn't bother me."

Beyond the boxing accolades, Warburton knows how much an upset victory over Adames would change his family's life.

"Win this and everything changes for my family, and I would probably become the mandatory challenger," he said.

"I've got someone in front of me who is at the highest level. To even be in the ring with him means I've completed boxing in a way, regardless of what happens.

"I'm a lad from north Wales who only had an ambition of winning a Welsh title. To step in with a world champion is what dreams are made of."
